clue.text: Crazily tearing round a Danube gorge

indicators.note: acting crazily, the letters of the word before it go wild and land in a new order

parts.note: a round thing is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone races madly around a famous river gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazily' rearranges TEARING together with O, the ring shape that 'round' gives. The Iron Gate is the gorge where the Danube cuts between Serbia and Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Gate is the name of the narrow gorge on the Danube between Serbia and Romania.

clue.text: Grass doing well, apparently

explanation.definitionFit: To grass is British slang for telling the police about someone; a person who is doing well seems to be on top form.

clue.text: Place for spectacles around the harbour

indicators.note: around tells us the pair of letters goes on either side of the harbour word

parts.note: two round lenses look like the letters OO
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: Somewhere to buy glasses near the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps OO, two letters that look like a pair of spectacles, round PORT. Oporto is the Portuguese city also called Porto.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is a city in northern Portugal, famous for port wine, so it is a location.

clue.text: Leave South to drink and talk

parts.note: to go is to leave
to sip is to drink in small amounts

explanation.surface: Someone heads south for a drink and a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is idle chatter about other people, light conversation.

clue.text: Line of business at sea

parts.note: a line of business usually means a job, but here it is a shipping lane used by merchant ships

explanation.walkthrough: 'Line of business' suggests a career; read literally it is a commercial path across the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchant ships follow established sea lanes for carrying goods, a path of commerce.

clue.text: Form of address

parts.note: reads like a polite way of naming someone, as 'Sir' or 'Madam', but an address can be a talk given to an audience

explanation.walkthrough: A 'form of address' sounds like a title such as 'Your Grace'; here an address is a talk delivered to a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: An address delivered to an audience is a formal talk, so it takes the shape of an oration.

clue.text: An apple first in importance after another fruit

indicators.note: after means the word for first in importance comes behind the fruit

parts.note: a pear is a fruit other than the apple
main means chief or most important

explanation.surface: An apple ranks top, beating a rival fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts MAIN behind PEAR. A pearmain is an old English apple variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearmain is the name of a group of old dessert apple varieties, such as Worcester Pearmain.

clue.text: Goes up, that is a change a from living close to the ground

indicators.note: a change of letters means the fodder words are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Something rises, which is a shift away from staying low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges GOES UP with IE. The stray 'a' after 'change' looks like a printing slip in the newspaper text.
explanation.definitionFit: Epigeous is a botanical term for plants growing on or near the soil surface.

clue.text: A common swinging hit a from a farm-hand?

explanation.definitionFit: A haymaker is a wild swinging punch in boxing, and also a farm worker who cuts and dries grass for fodder.

clue.text: On paper just the size for Touchstone

definitions.text: On paper just the size for Touchstone

parts.words: On paper just the size for Touchstone
parts.note: a standard paper size whose name, split up, is the headgear of a jester such as Touchstone

explanation.walkthrough: Touchstone is the court jester in Shakespeare's As You Like It, so a jester's cap would be just his size; the same name is an old British paper size.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a traditional large sheet size of writing paper, and a fool's cap is a jester's hat.

clue.text: Does he help to keep the household together?

definitions.text: Does he help to keep the household together?

parts.words: Does he help to keep the household together?
parts.note: pictures someone holding a ... together emotionally, but means a long-serving servant kept on by one household

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a peacemaking relative; the answer is a servant who has worked for a family for many years, 'retained' by them.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-standing domestic servant employed by one household is traditionally called this.

clue.text: See 10
Minute growth discovered by a doctor with Lincoln's backing

parts.note: MO stands for medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: backing means the name taken from Lincoln is read from right to left

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A tiny tumour is found by a physician, supported by a president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ABE, Abraham Lincoln's nickname, into EBA after A and MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled organism visible only under a microscope is a tiny living thing that grows and divides.

clue.text: Is no putrid concoction, albeit upsetting

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of the words before are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mixture that is not rotten, though still upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' rearranges IS NO PUTRID. 'upsetting' is the noun sense, the act of upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: Disruption is the act of throwing things into disorder, an upsetting of normal order.

clue.text: Concern for one over a hundred in loneliness

indicators.note: in tells us the pair of letters goes inside the word for loneliness

parts.note: solitude is being alone, close to loneliness

indicators.note: in an across clue, one placed over a hundred means it comes first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Worry for a lonely person amid a crowd of a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts I before C, and 'in' places IC inside SOLITUDE, after SOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Solicitude is anxious care for someone's welfare, a kind of worried attention.

clue.text: Steals up as a heart throb does

definitions.text: Steals up as a heart throb does

indicators.note: a heart throbbing is beating and moving, so the letters of the two words before are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone creeps up the way a heartbeat speeds.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of STEALS UP, set beating by the heart, rearrange; and a beating heart does exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulsate is to beat rhythmically, expanding and contracting like a heart.

clue.text: Fine form of punishment

explanation.definitionFit: Spanking means excellent or brisk, as in 'a spanking pace'; it is also smacking on the bottom as a penalty.

clue.text: Chat with girl producing a S something brilliant

indicators.note: producing something new from the words before means their letters are remade into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A conversation with a girl produces something dazzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producing' rearranges CHAT and GIRL. The 'a S' before 'something' looks like a printing slip in the newspaper text.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc light gives an intensely bright glare from an electric spark between electrodes.

clue.text: Floor of the brain?

parts.note: an upper floor of a house is slang for the head or mind, so the brain lives on this floor

explanation.walkthrough: Old slang calls the head the top floor of the body; this is the American spelling of storey.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper storey is informal slang for the head or intellect, the top level of a building.

clue.text: Russian composer with a connection in Georgia

indicators.note: in tells us the connection word sits inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a link is a connection

explanation.surface: A Russian musician with ties to Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LINK inside GA. Mikhail Glinka was a nineteenth-century Russian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Glinka wrote the opera A Life for the Tsar and is called the father of Russian classical music.

clue.text: Up from the country and pulled most of the way?

explanation.definitionFit: Being up in the city from the country means visiting the capital; a vehicle being towed is pulled, nearly all the way written as the phrase plus N.

clue.text: Very good man in part of the church

indicators.note: in tells us the good man is placed inside the other word

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword's standard good man

explanation.surface: A very good man is found in a section of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ST inside VERY, taken as written, after VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is a room in a church where vestments are kept and clergy robe.

clue.text: See nothing in being old and infirm

indicators.note: in tells us the word for nothing is placed inside the other word

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Being frail and elderly, one sees nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts NIL inside SEE, between its S and its last E. 'See' is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Senile describes the mental and bodily weakness that can come with great age.

clue.text: Clue open to promote amplitude

indicators.note: promoting something moves it about, here shifting the letters of the two words before into a new order

explanation.surface: An open clue is set to boost generosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to promote' rearranges the letters of CLUE and OPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth or abundance, and amplitude can mean plentifulness.

clue.text: Wooden actress?

explanation.definitionFit: Twiggy means made of or like small branches, so woody; Twiggy was the 1960s model who also acted on film.

clue.text: One forever on point duty

parts.note: point duty is a traffic officer's job of directing cars; this one points the way permanently at a junction

explanation.walkthrough: Point duty is a police officer directing traffic at a junction; the roadside post that points the way never goes off duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A post at a crossroads with arms pointing to places is always pointing travellers onward.

clue.text: They can be pleasant or abhorrent to look at

definitions.text: They can be pleasant or abhorrent to look at

parts.words: They can be pleasant or abhorrent to look at
parts.note: places tourists see are pleasant, while calling someone 'a fright' or 'a mess' is the abhorrent sense

explanation.walkthrough: The sights of a city are pleasant to visit, but 'you look a sight' means you look dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sights are things seen, from famous attractions to dreadful-looking spectacles.

clue.text: Lumbering in an ugly way

indicators.note: the way in which letters are arranged changes, so the words just before are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'way' signals that the letters of IN AN UGLY are taken another way, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy, awkward mover is lumbering, heavy and graceless.
